<!-- exmp-1: body_md -->
Let $n=1$, $V={\mathbb K}$, $\nabla =\partial_x + f(x)$ where $f(x)\in {\mathbb K}(x)$. Then
\bean
\label{ex1}
(\partial_x + f)^p = f^p+f^{(p-1)}.
\eean
<!-- end exmp-1 -->
<!-- exmp-2: body_md -->
\label{ex2}

Let $n=1$, $f(x)\in{\mathbb K}(x)$, $H(x) \in (\operatorname{End} V)(x)$.
Consider the three connections:
\bea
\nabla_f := \partial_x + f(x),
\qquad
\nabla_H := \partial_x + H(x),
\qquad
\nabla_{f\operatorname{Id}_V+H} := \partial_x + f(x)\operatorname{Id}_V +H\,.
\eea
Then the corresponding $p$-curvatures satisfy the relation:
\bean
\label{C-rel}
C_{f\operatorname{Id}_V+H} =C_f \operatorname{Id}_V + C_H\,.
\eean
Indeed, the third connection $\nabla_{f\operatorname{Id}_V+H}$ is identified with the tensor product of the first two connections:
$\nabla_f \otimes \operatorname{Id}_V + \operatorname{Id}_{\mathbb K}\otimes \nabla_H$. Then the $p$-curvature of the tensor-product connection
equals $C_f \otimes \operatorname{Id}_V + \operatorname{Id}_{\mathbb K}\otimes C_H$, which gives \eqref{C-rel}.
<!-- end exmp-2 -->
<!-- lem-1: body_md -->
\label{lem: tilde}
The $p$-curvature operators of $\nabla^o$ are given by the formulas:
\bean
\label{p l}
(\nabla_{t_l}^o)^p
&=&
\tilde \varphi_l,\qquad l=1,\dots,r,
\\
\label{p m}
(\nabla_{z_m}^o)^p
&=&
\tilde \psi_m, \qquad m=1,\dots,n,
\eean
where
\bean
\label{f l}
\tilde \varphi_l
&=&
\varphi_l^p + \partial_{t_l}^{p-1}(\varphi_l),
\\
\label{f m}
\tilde \psi_m
&=&
\psi_m^p + \partial_{z_m}^{p-1}(\psi_m).
\eean
Furthermore, each of the functions $(\varphi_l, \psi_m)$ is a function of
$(t^p,z^p) := (t_1^p,\dots, t_r^p, z_1^p, \dots, z_n^p)$.
<!-- end lem-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
Formulas \eqref{f l} and \eqref{f m} follow from \eqref{ex1}.

For any $l$ and $ m $, on the one hand, we have
\bea
[\nabla^o_{t_l}, (\nabla^o_{z_m})^p]=0,
\eea
and, on the other hand,
\bea
[\nabla^o_{t_l}, \tilde \psi_m] = \partial_{t_l}\tilde \psi_m\,.
\eea
Hence $\partial_{t_l}\tilde \psi_m=0$, and $\tilde \psi_m$, as a function of $t_l$, is a function of $t_l^p$.
The remainder of the lemma is proved similarly.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- lem-2: body_md -->
\label{lem Sto}
Let $(t^0,z^0)$ be a solution to the system \eqref{bae}.
Let $1\leqslant i\leqslant r$ and $g\in A_{(t^0,z^0)}$. Then
$\Delta \,\nabla^o_{t_i} (g)$
is the zero element of $A_{(t^0,z^0)}$.
<!-- end lem-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
We have
\bea
\Delta \, \nabla^o_{t_i} (g)
=\left(\nabla^o_{t_i}\right)^p
\left(\prod_{j\ne i}^r \left(\nabla^o_{t_j}\right)^{p-1}\right) (g)
= \tilde \varphi_i \cdot
\left(\prod_{j\ne i}^r \left(\nabla^o_{t_j}\right)^{p-1}\right) (g).
\eea
By Lemma \ref{lem: tilde}, $\tilde \varphi_i$ is a function of $(t^p,z^p)$. Because we are operating in the quotient $A_{(t^0,z^0)}$ defined by $\mathcal J_p$, the $p$-th powers of the variables are constant: $t_l^p \equiv (t_l^0)^p$ and $z_m^p \equiv (z_m^0)^p$. Thus, $\tilde \varphi_i$ reduces to the constant $\tilde \varphi_i(t^0,z^0)$, which is zero by the assumption that $(t^0,z^0)$ solves the Bethe ansatz equations. Therefore, $\tilde \varphi_i$ induces the zero element in $A_{(t^0,z^0)}$.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- thm-1: body_md -->
\label{thm eig}

Let $(t^0, z^0)$ be a solution to the system of Bethe ansatz equations:
\bean
\label{BEA}
\tilde \varphi_l(t,z) = 0,
\qquad l=1,\dots,r.
\eean
Then the element $I \in V\otimes A_{(t^0,z^0)}$ is a flat section of the extended connection. That is,
\bean
\label{fecl}
\left(\partial_{z_m}+ \psi_m + H_m\right) I
&=&
0,\qquad m=1,\dots, n,
\\
\label{fecm}
\left(\partial_{t_l}+ \varphi_l\right) I
&=&
0,\qquad l=1,\dots, r.
\eean
Furthermore, the element $I $ is an eigensection of the $p$-curvature operators $(C_m)$
with respective eigenvalues $(-\tilde \psi_m(t^0,z^0))$, that is,
\begin{equation}
\label{eigv}
C_m\,I \,=\, -\, \tilde \psi_m(t^0,z^0)\, I, \qquad m=1,\dots,n.
\end{equation}
<!-- end thm-1 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
Applying $\Delta$ to both sides of equation \eqref{IR}, we obtain
\bean
\label{2.13}
\left(\partial_{z_m}+ \psi_m + H_m\right)I
=
\sum_{l=1}^r \,\tilde \varphi_l\cdot \left(\prod_{j\ne l}^r \left(\nabla^o_{t_j}\right)^{p-1}\right) \!
\left(g_{l,m}\right),
\eean
where $ \tilde \varphi_l $ acts as the zero element in $A_{(t^0,z^0)}$. Formula \eqref{fecl} is proved.

We have
\bea
\nabla^o_{t_l} I = \left(\nabla^o_{t_l}\right)^p \left(\prod_{j\ne l} \left(\nabla^o_{t_j}\right)^{p-1}\right) (w)
=\tilde \varphi_l \cdot \left(\prod_{j\ne l} \left(\nabla^o_{t_j}\right)^{p-1}\right) \!(w).
\eea
This element is zero in $V \otimes A_{(t^0,z^0)}$ since $\tilde \varphi_l$ is zero in $A_{(t^0,z^0)}$.
This proves formula \eqref{fecm}.

Applying $\left(\partial_{z_m}+ \psi_m + H_m\right) ^{p-1}$ to formula \eqref{fecl} yields
\bea
0=\left(\partial_{z_m}+ \psi_m + H_m\right)^p I =
\left(C_m + \tilde \psi_m\right )I,
\eea
where $\tilde \psi_m$ equals the constant $\tilde \psi_m(t^0,z^0)$ in $A_{(t^0,z^0)}$ since
$\tilde \psi_m$ is a function of $(t^p,z^p)$. This proves formula \eqref{eigv}. Theorem \ref{thm eig} is proved.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- cor-1: body_md -->
\label{cor eig}

Let $(t^0, z^0)$ be a solution to the system of Bethe ansatz equations \eqref{BEA}.
Then the vector $I(t^0,z^0) \in V$ is an eigenvector of the $p$-curvature operators $(C_m(z^0))$
with respective eigenvalues $(-\tilde \psi_m(t^0,z^0))$, that is,
\bea
C_m(z^0)\,I(t^0,z^0) \,=\, -\, \tilde \psi_m(t^0,z^0)\, I(t^0,z^0), \qquad m=1,\dots,n.
\eea
<!-- end cor-1 -->
<!-- lem-3: body_md -->
\label{lem dit}

If $i_1+\dots+ i_r>0$, then $c_{i_1,\dots, i_r, k_1,\dots,k_n} = 0$. In other words, the ratio
$R_j$ does not depend on $t$,
and the direction of the element $I$ depends on $z$ only.
<!-- end lem-3 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
By formula \eqref{fecm}, the standard derivative in the quotient satisfies $\partial_{t_l}I = -\varphi_l I$. Because $\varphi_l$ is a scalar function, this implies $\partial_{t_l}I_j = -\varphi_l I_j$ for all components $j$.
Applying the quotient rule, we obtain
\bea
\partial_{t_l}R_j = \frac{\left(\partial_{t_l} I_j\right) I_{j_0} - I_j \left(\partial_{t_l}I_{j_0}\right)}{I_{j_0}^2} = \frac{(-\varphi_l I_j) I_{j_0} - I_j (-\varphi_l I_{j_0})}{I_{j_0}^2} = 0.
\eea
Since $\partial_{t_l} R_j \equiv 0$ in $A_{(t^0,z^0)}$ for all $l=1,\dots,r$, and the quotient ideal only restricts powers greater than or equal to $p$, all coefficients in $R_j$ involving strictly positive powers of $(t_l - t_l^0)$ must be zero.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- thm-2: body_md -->
\label{thm global}

 Assume that 
\eqref{p-c=0} holds, and $\Phi$ is a master function.
Define  $J \in V\otimes {\mathbb K}(t,z)$ by the formula:
\bean
\label{elt J}
J = \Phi \,I =\Phi \,\Delta (w)  = \left(\prod_{i=1}^l \partial_{t_i}^{p-1} \right)(\Phi \,w).
\eean 
 Then $J$ is a flat section of $\nabla$\,:
\bean
\label{fsP}
\left(\partial_{z_m} + H_m\right) J=0, \qquad m=1,\dots, n,
\eean
and also
\bean
\label{t-fl}
\partial_{t_l}J=0, \qquad l=1,\dots,r.
\eean
<!-- end thm-2 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Equation \eqref{fecl} holds for any values of $(t,z)$ since \eqref{p-c=0} holds.
Multiplying both sides of \eqref{fecl} by $\Phi$ we obtain
\bean
0=\Phi \left(\partial_{z_m}+ \psi_m + H_m\right) I = \left(\partial_{z_m} +H_m\right) \Phi I.
\eean
This proves \eqref{fsP}. Equation \eqref{t-fl} follows similarly from \eqref{fecm}.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- lem-4: body_md -->
The connection $\nabla^o$ is flat.
<!-- end lem-4 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
The proof is by inspection.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- lem-5: body_md -->
The $p$-curvature operators of $\nabla^o$ are given by the formulas:
\bea
(\nabla_{t_l}^o)^p
&=&
\frac 1{\kappa^p}\,
\tilde \varphi_l,\qquad l=1,\dots,r,
\\
(\nabla_{z_m}^o)^p
&=&
\frac 1{\kappa^p}\,
\tilde \psi_m, \qquad m=1,\dots,n,
\eea
where
\bean
\label{tikz}
\tilde \varphi_l
&=&
 \sum_{m=1}^n \frac{-h_p(\Lambda_m)}{t_l^p-z_m^p} + \sum_{j\ne l} \frac {h_p(2)}{t_l^p-t_j^p}
\,, \quad l=1,\dots,r\,,
\\
\notag
\tilde \psi_m
&=&
 \sum_{l=1}^r \frac {-h_p(\Lambda_m)}{z_m^p-t_l^p}+ \sum_{i\ne m} \frac{h_p(\Lambda_m\Lambda_i/2)}{z_m^p-z_i^p} 
 \,, \quad
m=1,\dots,n\,.
\eean
<!-- end lem-5 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
The lemma follows from formula \eqref{ex1}.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- thm-3: body_md -->
\label{thm ri}

There exist $V$-valued rational functions $g_{l,m}(t,z)$, for $l=1,$ \dots, $r$ and $m=1,\dots,n$, such that these functions, together with the rank-one connection $\nabla^o$ defined by \eqref{kzoo}
and the weight function $w$ defined by \eqref{Wkz},
give an integral representation of the KZ connection $\nabla$ defined by \eqref{kz}.
That is,
\bean
\label{Irr}
\left(\nabla^o_{z_m} + \frac 1\kappa H_m\right)\!(w)
&=&
\sum_{l=1}^r \nabla^o_{t_l}\left(g_{l,m}\right), \qquad m=1,\dots,n.
\eean
<!-- end thm-3 -->
<!-- thm-4: body_md -->
\label{thm ei}

Let $(t^0, z^0)$ be a solutions to the system of Bethe ansatz equations:
\bean
\label{Bea}
\sum_{m=1}^n \frac{-h_p(\Lambda_m)}{t_l^p-z_m^p} + \sum_{j\ne l} \frac {h_p(2)}{t_l^p-t_j^p}\,=\,0
\,, \quad l=1,\dots,r\,.
\eean
Then the element $I \in V\otimes A_{(t^0,z^0)}$ is a flat section of the extended connection. That is,
\bea
\left(\partial_{z_m}+ \frac 1\kappa \psi_m +\frac 1\kappa H_m\right) I
&=&
0,\qquad m=1,\dots, n,
\\
\left(\partial_{t_l}+\frac 1\kappa \varphi_l\right) I
&=&
0,\qquad l=1,\dots, r.
\eea
Furthermore, the element $I$ is an eigensection of the $p$-curvature operators $(C_m)$ of the connection $\nabla$
with respective eigenvalues $(-\frac 1\kappa\tilde \psi_m(t^0,z^0))$, that is,
\begin{equation}
\label{igv}
C_m\,I \,=\, - \frac 1{\kappa^p}
\left( \sum_{l=1}^r \frac {-h_p(\Lambda_m)}{(z_m^0)^p-(t_l^0)^p}+ \sum_{i\ne m}
\frac{h_p(\Lambda_m\Lambda_i/2)}{(z_m^0)^p-(z_i^0)^p} \right) I, \qquad m=1,\dots,n.
\end{equation}
<!-- end thm-4 -->
<!-- cor-2: body_md -->
\label{cor ig}

Let $(t^0, z^0)$ be a solution to the system of Bethe ansatz equations \eqref{Bea}.
Then the vector $I(t^0,z^0) \in V$ is an eigenvector of the $p$-curvature operators $(C_m(z^0))$
with respective eigenvalues $(-\tilde \psi_m(t^0,z^0))$. That is,
\bea
C_m(z^0)\,I(t^0,z^0) \,=\, -\, \frac 1\kappa\tilde \psi_m(t^0,z^0)\, I(t^0,z^0), \qquad m=1,\dots,n.
\eea
<!-- end cor-2 -->
<!-- rem-1: body_md -->
In \cite{EV2}, the spectrum of the $p$-curvature operators of periodic pencils of flat connections is described.
The KZ connection \eqref{kz} is an example of a periodic pencil of flat connections. Formula \eqref{igv} for the eigenvalues of the $p$-curvature operators agrees with the dscription in \cite{EV2}.

Eigenvectors and eigenvalues of the $p$-curvature operators, as well as the $p$-curvature operators
themselves, are described in \cite{VV1} in the special case when $r=1$ and $\Lambda_m=1$ for $m=1,\dots, n$.
<!-- end rem-1 -->
<!-- thm-5: body_md -->
\label{thm sing}
There exist
$\left(\bigotimes^n_{j=1} M_{{\Lambda_j}}\right)\left[\<\>\sum_{j=1}^n\Lambda_j-2r+2\right]$-valued
functions $h_l(t,z)$ for $l=1,\dots,r$, rational in variables $(t,z)$, such that
\bean
\label{Si}
e\, w \,= \,
\sum_{l=1}^r \nabla^o_{t_l}\left(h_{l}\right).
\eean
<!-- end thm-5 -->
<!-- cor-3: body_md -->
\label{cor sing}
The element $I$ of Theorem \ref{thm ei} lies in
\bea
{\operatorname{Sing}} \left(\bigotimes^n_{j=1} M_{{\Lambda_j}}\right)\left[\<\>\sum_{j=1}^n\Lambda_j-2r\<\>\right]\otimes A_{(t^0,z^0)}.
\eea
<!-- end cor-3 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
We have
\bea
e\, I
=
\sum_{l=1}^r \left(\nabla^o_{t_l}\right)^p
\left(\prod_{j\ne l}^r \left(\nabla^o_{t_j}\right)^{p-1}\right) \!\!
\left(h_{l}\right)
= \sum_{l=1}^r \tilde \varphi_l \cdot \left(\prod_{j\ne l}^r \left(\nabla^o_{t_j}\right)^{p-1}\right) \!\!
\left(h_{l}\right) = 0.
\eea
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- lem-6: body_md -->
If $g\in{\mathbb K}(t,z)$, then
\bean
\label{ndc}
\Phi \nabla^o_{t_l}(f) = \partial_{t_l}(\Phi f),
\qquad
\Phi \nabla^o_{z_m}(f) = \partial_{z_m}(\Phi f),
\eean
for all $l,\,m$.
<!-- end lem-6 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
The proof is by inspection.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- thm-6: body_md -->
\label{thm Lau}
For any $l_1,\dots,l_r\in {\mathbb Z}_{\geqslant 0}$, the $V$-valued polynomial
$Q_{pl_1+p-1,\dots,\>pl_r+p-1}(z)$ is a flat section
of the KZ connection \eqref{kz},
\bean
\label{flat lp}
\left(\partial_{z_m}
\,+ \,\frac 1\kappa \,H_m\right)
Q_{pl_1+p-1,\dots,\>pl_r+p-1}\,=\,0, \quad m=1,\dots,n.
\eean
Furthermore, the polynomial $Q_{pl_1+p-1,\dots,\>pl_r+p-1}(z)$ is an eigensection of the
$p$-curvature operators with
all eigenvalues equal to 0, that is
\bean
\label{7.4}
C_{m}(z) \,Q_{pl_1+p-1,\dots,\>pl_r+p-1}(z) = 0,
\quad m=1,\dots,n.
\eean
We also have
\bean
\label{7.5}
e \, Q_{pl_1+p-1,\dots,\>pl_r+p-1}(z)= 0.
\eean
<!-- end thm-6 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
By Theorem \ref{thm global}, the function
\bean
\label{JP}
J = \left(\prod_{i=1}^l \partial_{t_i}^{p-1} \right)(\Phi \,w) = 
-\sum_{l_1,\dots,l_r\geqslant 0}
Q_{pl_1+p-1,\dots,\>pl_r+p-1}(z)\,t_1^{pl_1}\dots t_r^{pl_r}
\eean
satisfies 
\bea
\left(\partial_{z_m}
\,+ \,\frac 1\kappa \,H_m\right) J\,=\,0, \quad m=1,\dots,n.
\eea
This implies \eqref{flat lp}. The other claims of the theorem are clear.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- rem-2: body_md -->
The statement that the polynomials $Q_{pl_1+p-1,\dots,\>pl_r+p-1}(z)$ are flat sections of the KZ connection was proved in \cite{SV2} by a different construction. The polynomials
\\
$Q_{pl_1+p-1,\dots,\>pl_r+p-1}$ are called the $p$-hypergeometric flat sections.
<!-- end rem-2 -->
<!-- exmp-3: body_md -->
Let $r=1$ and $n=2g+1$ for some positive integer $g$. Let $\Lambda_m=1$ for $m=1,\dots,n$. Let $\kappa=2$. Then
\bea
\Phi &=& 
\prod_{i<j} (z_i-z_j)^{\overline{1/4}}
\prod_{m=1}^n (t_1-z_m)^{(p-1)/2}\,,
\\
w &=& \sum_{j=1}^n \frac 1{t_1-z_j} v_1\otimes \dots \otimes fv_1\otimes \dots \otimes v_1\,,
\eea
where $fv_1$ stays at the $j$th position. Then Theorem \ref{thm Lau} produces $g$
\ $p$-hypergeometric flat sections $Q_{p-1}$, $Q_{2p-1}$, \dots, $Q_{gp-1}$.

\vsk.2>

It is shown in \cite{VV1}, that these solutions span all rational flat section of the KZ connection in this case, see also \cite{VV2}.
<!-- end exmp-3 -->
<!-- lem-7: body_md -->
The connection $\nabla^o$ is flat.
<!-- end lem-7 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
The proof is by inspection.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- lem-8: body_md -->
The $p$-curvature operators of $\nabla^o$ are given by the formulas:
\bea
(\nabla_{t_l}^o)^p
&=&
\frac 1{\kappa^p}\tilde \varphi_l,\qquad l=1,\dots,r,
\\
(\nabla_{z_m}^o)^p
&=&
\frac 1{\kappa^p}\tilde \varphi_l, \qquad m=1,\dots,n+1,
\eea
where
\bea
\tilde \varphi_l
&=&
-\lambda^p + \sum_{m=1}^n \frac{-h_p(\Lambda_m)}{t_l^p-z_m^p} + \sum_{j\ne l} \frac {h_p(2)}{t_l^p-t_j^p}
\,, \quad l=1,\dots,r\,,
\\
\tilde \psi_m
&=&
 \frac {\lambda^p} 2 + \sum_{l=1}^r \frac {-h_p(\Lambda_m)}{z_m^p-t_l^p}+ \sum_{i\ne m} \frac{h_p(\Lambda_m\Lambda_i/2)}{z_m^p-z_i^p}\,, \quad
m=1,\dots,n\,,
\\
\tilde \psi_{n+1}
&=&
 \frac 1 2\, \sum_{m=1}^nz_m^p - \sum_{l=1}^r t_l^p\,.
\eea
<!-- end lem-8 -->
<!-- thm-7: body_md -->
\label{thm ir}

There exist $V$-valued rational functions $g_{l,m}(t,z,\lambda)$, for $l=1,$ \dots, $r$ and $m=1,\dots,n+1$, such that these functions, together with the rank-one connection $\nabla^o$ defined by \eqref{kzdo}
and the weight function $w$ defined by \eqref{Wkz},
give an integral representation of the compatible KZ and dynamical connections
$\nabla$ defined by \eqref{kzd}.
That is,
\bean
\label{IRR}
\left(\nabla^o_{z_m} +\frac 1\kappa H_m\right)\!(w)
&=&
\sum_{l=1}^r \nabla^o_{t_l}\left(g_{l,m}\right), \qquad m=1,\dots,n,
\\
\notag
\left(\nabla^o_{\lambda} + \frac 1\kappa D\right)\!(w)
&=&
\sum_{l=1}^r \nabla^o_{t_l}\left(g_{l,n+1}\right).
\eean
<!-- end thm-7 -->
<!-- thm-8: body_md -->
Let $(t^0, z^0, \lambda^0)$ be a solution to the system of Bethe ansatz equations:
\bean
\label{bbea}
-\lambda^p + \sum_{m=1}^n \frac{-h_p(\Lambda_m)}{t_l^p-z_m^p} + \sum_{j\ne l} \frac {h_p(2)}{t_l^p-t_j^p}\,=\,0
\,, \quad l=1,\dots,r\,.
\eean
Then the element $I \in V\otimes A_{(t^0,z^0,\lambda^0)}$ is a flat section of the extended connection. That is,
\bea
\left(\partial_{z_m}+ \frac 1\kappa\psi_m +\frac1\kappa H_m\right) I
&=&
0,\qquad m=1,\dots, n,
\\
\left(\partial_{\lambda}+ \frac 1\kappa \psi_{n+1} +\frac 1\kappa D\right) I
&=&
0,
\\
\left(\partial_{t_l}+ \frac 1\kappa\varphi_l\right) I
&=&
0,\qquad l=1,\dots, r.
\eea
Furthermore, the element $I$ is an eigensection of the $p$-curvature operators $(C_m)$
of the connection $\nabla$
with respective eigenvalues $(-\frac 1\kappa \tilde \psi_m(t^0,z^0,\lambda^0))$. That is,
\bean
\label{igvV}
C_m\,I \,
&=&\, - \frac 1{\kappa^p}
\left( \frac {\left(\lambda^0\right)^p} 2 + \sum_{l=1}^r \frac {-h_p(\Lambda_m)}{(z_m^0)^p-(t_l^0)^p}+ \sum_{i\ne m}
\frac{h_p(\Lambda_m\Lambda_i/2)}{(z_m^0)^p-(z_i^0)^p} \right) I, \ m=1,\dots,n,
\\
\label{Dc}
\phantom{aaaa}
C_{n+1}\,I \,&=&\,
- \frac 1{\kappa^p} \left(\frac 1 2\, \sum_{m=1}^n(z_m^0)^p - \sum_{l=1}^r (t_l^0)^p\right) I\,.
\eean
<!-- end thm-8 -->
<!-- cor-4: body_md -->
\label{cor last}

Let $(t^0, z^0, \lambda^0)$ be a solutions to the system of Bethe ansatz equations \eqref{bbea}.
Then the vector $I(t^0,z^0,\lambda^0) \in V$ is an eigenvector of the $p$-curvature operators $(C_m(z^0,\lambda^0))$
of the connection $\nabla$
with respective eigenvalues $(-\frac 1\kappa\tilde \psi_m(t^0,z^0,\lambda^0))$. That is,
\bean
\label{igv l}
&&
C_m(z^0,\lambda^0)\,I(t^0,z^0,\lambda^0) \,
\\
\notag
&&
= \, - \frac 1{\kappa^p}
\left( \frac {\left(\lambda^0\right)^p} 2 + \sum_{l=1}^r \frac {-h_p(\Lambda_m)}{(z_m^0)^p-(t_l^0)^p}
+ \sum_{i\ne m}
\frac{h_p(\Lambda_m\Lambda_i/2)}{(z_m^0)^p-(z_i^0)^p} \right) I(t^0,z^0,\lambda^0), \ m=1,\dots,n,
\\
\label{Dc l}
\phantom{aaa}
&&
C_{n+1}(z^0,\lambda^0)\,I(t^0,z^0,\lambda^0)
\\
\notag
&& \,=\,
- \frac 1{\kappa^p} \left(\frac 1 2\, \sum_{m=1}^n(z_m^0)^p - \sum_{l=1}^r (t_l^0)^p\right) I(t^0,z^0,\lambda^0)\,.
\eean
<!-- end cor-4 -->
